## The Recipe {#ruth .hook data-milestone="1930-08" transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

```{=html}
<div class="fill fill--center tl-content">
<!-- the first beat's tag: the recipe → the cookbook → the store shelf (the playbook calls these back) -->

<div class="img-grid">
  <figure>
    <img src="images/ruth-wakefield.webp" alt="Ruth Wakefield">
    <figcaption>
      <span class="cap-title">Ruth</span>
      <span class="cap-sub">A dietitian with a kitchen and an idea</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="fragment">
    <img src="images/toll-house-inn.webp" alt="The Toll House Inn">
    <figcaption>
      <span class="cap-title">The Inn</span>
      <span class="cap-sub">Whitman, Massachusetts, 1930</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <figure class="fragment">
    <img src="images/chocolate-chip-cookie.jpg" alt="A plate of chocolate chip cookies">
    <figcaption>
      <span class="cap-title">The Cookie</span>
      <span class="cap-sub">One kitchen, one baker.</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>
</div>

<div class="tl-static" aria-hidden="true">
  <div class="tl-static__track">
    <div class="tl-static__fill" style="width:6%; background:var(--soil);"></div>
    <div class="tl-static__marker" style="left:calc(6% - 11px); background:var(--soil);"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="tl-static__labels">
    <span style="left:6%;  color:var(--text);">Aug 1930</span>
```

::: {.notes}
**Tanya:** Ruth Wakefield ran an inn in Whitman, Massachusetts. **[click: the Inn]** She was a dietitian, she had a kitchen, and one day she had an idea: chop up a chocolate bar and put it in the cookie dough.

**[click: the cookie]** Guests loved it. It was a hit. And it existed in exactly one place: her kitchen. If you wanted the cookie, you drove to the inn.
:::

## The Cookbook {#cookbook .hook data-milestone="1938-10" transition="fade" transition-speed="fast"}

```{=html}
<div class="fill fill--center tl-content">
<div class="hook-split">
  <div class="hook-split__media">
    <img class="img-object" src="images/toll-house-cookbook.jpg" alt="Ruth Wakefield's Toll House Tried and True Recipes cookbook">
  </div>
  <div class="hook-split__aside beat">
    <div class="beat__eyebrow">The cookbook</div>
    <h3 class="beat__headline">The recipe is published.</h3>
    <p class="beat__consequence fragment">Anyone who can bake.</p>
  </div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="tl-static" aria-hidden="true">
  <div class="tl-static__track">
    <div class="tl-static__fill" style="width:50%; background:var(--soil);"></div>
    <div class="tl-static__marker" style="left:calc(50% - 11px); background:var(--soil);"></div>

  <div class="tl-static__labels">

```

::: {.notes}
**Tanya:** Eight years later she published the recipe. **[click: the consequence]** Now anyone could make it. Anyone who owned an oven, had flour and butter in the house, and knew what "cream the sugar" meant.

Which is a lot of people. It's also not everyone.
:::

**Tanya:** Then Nestlé put it in the grocery store. **[click: the consequence]** Ready-to-bake dough. No recipe, no measuring, no mixing. Slice it, pop it in the oven, and eat it.

**Jadey:** So. What does a cookie have to do with a technical talk at posit::conf?
